key_points.point: Strong vanna and charm option flows will structurally support the market unless equities decline sharply enough to trigger put risk.
Holiday light-volume periods compress volatility and accelerate time decay, strengthening market-supportive options flows through year-end.
The market is expected to hold up sideways to higher into mid-December, with a more substantial market decline coming in January.
End-of-month portfolio rebalancing flows are expected to be mildly positive, though small compared to options market flows.
Options positions should sell December OpEx volatility and own calendar-spread volatility expiring in January, February, or March.
Fixed-strike downside put volatility is elevated, making net volatility purchases unattractive until after mid-December OpEx.
Any market pullbacks ahead of year-end are likely to be orderly stair-step declines rather than a panic crash due to dealer positioning.

This is the fat pitch we have patiently been waiting for, and we're not going to miss it. Markets bottom on bad news and deleveraging. We have had a lot of both.

Our sentiment indicator reached −1.6 and the VIX hit 36, matching December 2018, with hedge fund positioning similarly washed out. While the S&P broke below our 7,100–7,300 range, we view this as an overshoot of fair value and remain constructive into 2027

Valuations Support Adding Exposure. The S&P 500 trades at 16.4x versus our 19–19.6x fair value range, a discount of roughly three multiple turns even after accounting for rates. The Nasdaq 100 is below 17x and its COVID valuation trough
Bottom line, we reiterate our constructive view on 2027 but with a much more bullish tactical view now given the capitulation witnessed last week and attractive valuation levels
